speaker: parent_unspecified
quote: I was really hoping to use my last week or so or prepartum leave to relax and feel restored. Instead I’m tired and disabled and feel like someone is dragging me across sandpaper to the finish line, but the finish line is another marathon.
context: A week before a planned birth, joint pain leaves her unable to rest on pre-birth leave.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: We made a big registry because none of our family lives anywhere near us, and they all want to help as much as possible.
context: 16 weeks, first baby; asks if sending the registry link now is too early.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: is it reasonable to send out our registry link now (16 wks) since none of them are going to be here for a baby shower and it gives us a lot of time to fill in and buy things that people don't purchase? Or should we still wait until like the third trimester?
context: Timing question about registry with distant family.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: I'm single, and only get 2 weeks off work, so I'm trying to work up until I have this baby.
context: 39+5 with her third; tornado-damaged workplace offers a far-away night shift or a short local one.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: I can either go into work at 1am, and take a shuttle an hour away (just over an hour from my hospital), and get back around 10am. I'd be paid for the whole time, but I won't have access to my own vehicle, and I can't take my phone (or my hospital bag) with me.
context: Choosing between pay and being near her hospital days before her due date.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: Seems like the safer option, but I'm making much less money that way.
context: The shorter local shift near her hospital pays far less.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I knew I didn’t want to move because I was leaving my mom, who lived only 30 minutes away and was a huge part of my support system.
context: 12 weeks, moved out of state for her husband's new job three weeks earlier.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I work remotely, so I’m home by myself all day in a house that doesn’t feel like home yet. I’m having such a difficult time staying motivated to work. Every day I have moments where I cry, and mornings are by far the hardest.
context: Newly moved, first pregnancy, husband now away every weekday.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: On Saturday I pushed myself to try a Fit4Mom class, and I’m really glad I went because I met some nice people.
context: First attempt to meet people after moving; she cried when the instructor called her brave.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I worry about coming on too strong with people because I’m desperate for connection, and I don’t want to overwhelm new neighbors or the people I’m meeting.
context: Lonely after moving away from her support system.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I’m almost 11 weeks and the fatigue is taking over I feel like sleeping beauty without the beauty so I want to call in tomorrow. But i’m a store manager and feel so guilty about it.
context: Asks whether others call in sick for pregnancy symptoms.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I’m just afraid of not leading by example the way I should be it’s so frustrating
context: Trusts her staff to cover; the guilt is about her role as manager.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I’m EXTREMELY afraid of needles, my body immediately goes into what I can only describe as shock and starts shaking violently anytime I have to have one and I cry and sweat. It’s childish I know I’m trying to work on it lol.
context: Dreading routine blood draws at her 12-week appointment.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I want to get the NIPT done but I’m also afraid the results are going to give me more anxiety.
context: Weighing an optional blood test at 12 weeks.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I’m terrified to give birth as a first time mom who has a low pain tolerance. I also have a hard time adjusting to change despite knowing my whole life I’ve wanted to be a mom. I feel ready but also not at all. I can’t stop crying.
context: 38 weeks, a week before a scheduled induction.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I can’t wait to meet my son, but I’m so scared of post partum.
context: One week before her induction date.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I preferred to go into labor naturally, but for the health of my baby I’m willing to get induced despite hearing so many mixed opinions.
context: Scheduled induction at 39 weeks for a pregnancy condition.

speaker: new_mother
quote: They will say it’s hard but “it’s all worth it” — I get why people say it, but it doesn’t actually tell you anything. It’s not a warning, it’s a way to end the conversation. It’s what people say instead of telling you the truth.
context: Vent titled 'I feel blindsided' from a new mother.

speaker: new_mother
quote: Nobody tells you how much you’ll miss your old life either. Not the going-out, party version, just… being a person. Finishing a shower. Eating food while it’s hot.
context: New mother on what no one warned her about.

speaker: new_mother
quote: What actually gets me the most is other women not warning each other. I feel betrayed by my gender.
context: Blames other mothers for passing down a rosy script.

speaker: new_mother
quote: I used to say “a maternity leave would be nice” like it was some kind of break. I feel dumb saying that now. This is not a break.
context: Looking back at what she thought leave would be.

speaker: new_mother
quote: Breastfeeding wrecked me in a way I wasn’t ready for either. It’s not the peaceful bonding thing people show in photos.
context: Part of her list of things nobody prepared her for.

speaker: new_mother
quote: sometimes I hear women say pregnancy was wonderful while also describing how much support they had. And I can’t help thinking: if it was so great, how much of that was because you had people helping you through it?
context: Follow-up reply in her own thread.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: Everyone told me that I looked so pretty and that you couldn’t even tell I had a baby 6 weeks ago. I just didn’t feel like that, I feel postpartum.
context: Six weeks after her second birth, made up for her sister's wedding.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: Is there any chance for me have a natural birth this go around? Is it worth it?
context: Previous surgical birth six years earlier.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: They never offered (nobody did really lol) to come help with anything I would need to get done before baby comes either. It just makes me feel like they want to use me one last time before I have my baby
context: A week before her due date a friend asks for unpaid design help.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: There are apps out there that scan products and tell you what is or is not recommended for pregnant people to eat/ use. I already feel the anxiety taking over my life.
context: 5 weeks, first pregnancy, ten days before her first appointment.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I want to maintain my sanity, but of course I don’t want to do anything dangerous to my baby. Any reliable resources/ apps/ words of wisdom??
context: Overwhelmed by food and skincare avoidance lists at 5 weeks.
